note: EMPTY, and that is a statement about the 9 guards in tools/dev/anti-vacuity-cases.json. Swept 2026-08-30 over the whole population, not a sample. 177 test files scan the tree; 164 also state a zero-verdict (146 under the census's spellings plus 18 that used a spelling the census did not recognise until this sweep widened it). Removing guards whose only corpus is a directory they created themselves leaves 89 in scope. Four lenses, each answering a question the one before it could not. (1) Blank the bound corpus root. (2) Blank that root's test files too, since a guard whose corpus IS test files sees an untouched tree under lens 1. (3) Blank EVERY root at once, so no inferred binding can explain a pass, and record how much of the tree SURVIVED — a green over a tree the guard's own imports refilled is the instrument having no verdict, not the guard having none. (4) Judge a TEST rather than a file, comparing `expect()` calls between the blanked and intact arms: a test that passes over an empty listing while making strictly fewer assertions asserted less because there was less to assert. Lens 4 exists because lens 3 could not see `cross-slice-cycle`: its bans are LOOP BODIES over `readdir`, and the file's other tests throw on a blanked tree, so the file read RED while two vacuous tests sat inside it. Note also that removing a directory and emptying it are DIFFERENT probes — a missing directory makes `readdir` throw (the guard is safe), a present-but-empty one makes it return `[]` (the guard is vacuous), and only the second reproduces this defect. Result: 67 red (proven non-vacuous), 13 that throw when their corpus is absent, 9 green that are all instrument limits — 6 refilled by their own import closure, 1 whose corpus is the git index, 1 whose corpus is the host filesystem (`/sbin`), 1 whose corpus is `.github/workflows` and which was then proven non-vacuous by blanking that directory directly. Real findings: THREE — `no-leftover-backup-files` (floor on the tracked list but not on the `existsSync` narrowing) and two loop-body bans in `cross-slice-cycle`. All fixed, each with a paired control. This CORRECTS an earlier note reporting '16 more vacuous guards' from an interrupted partial sweep: every one was a lens artifact. A single blanked root cannot tell 'the guard noticed nothing' from 'the root it actually reads was left standing'.
